name: Tesaka Malagasy
world_status: a description exists but is not accessible

earlier_scan.verdict: a source was named but could not be reached
earlier_scan.source_named: Deschamps, Hubert. 1936. Le dialecte antaisaka (langue malgache). Tananarive: Pitot de la Beaujardiere.

sources.citation: Raoniarisoa, Noro. 1990. Accent and intonation in a Malagasy dialect. PhD thesis, Bangor University.
sources.access_detail: a digital copy (available on request); access check: open copy online
sources.note: Instrumental study of Malagasy word accent with listeners from several dialects; would supersede the older general statements if it reports Tesaka speakers (dialect not named in the abstract).

sources.citation: Ferrand, Gabriel. 1909. Essai de phonétique comparée du malais et des dialectes malgaches. Paris: Geuthner. Ch. VI 'L'accent tonique', pp. 236-245.
sources.note: General (Merina-based) Malagasy accent rules; 'Dialecte Antesaka' is no. 12 in the dialect list and Antesaka forms appear in segmental correspondence tables, but no Antesaka-specific accent statement.

Reference list only: Dez 1963, Vérin/Kottak/Gorlin 1969, Serva et al. 2012, Serva & Pasquini 2020, ISO CR 2010-035, Deschamps 1936 (x2), Elle 1905. No grammar/phonology-typed reference (Glottolog lists no grammar, sketch or phonology).

sources.citation: Serva, Maurizio & Michele Pasquini. 2020. Dialects of Madagascar. PLoS ONE 15(10): e0240170.
sources.note: Lexicostatistics on 207-item Swadesh lists including Antaisaka varieties; no mention of stress, accent or prosody.

sources.citation: Howe, Penelope. 2017. Tonogenesis in Central dialects of Malagasy. PhD, Rice University. Sec. 2.3.6 'Stress', pp. 48-49.
sources.note: General Malagasy rule (penultimate; antepenultimate on words with weak final -ka/-tra/-na; a few final-stressed) with notes for western/southwestern, North Betsimisaraka and Tsimihety; Taisaka is cited only for segmental facts from Dahl 1952 (e/i merger post-tonically, prenasalized voiceless merger). No Taisaka stress statement.

sources.citation: Bouwer, Leoni E. 2010. A bibliographic journey through Madagascar. SIL Language and Culture Documentation and Description 13.
sources.note: SIL bibliography grouped by ethnie; would reveal any unlisted Antaisaka linguistic/orthography materials (SIL Madagascar did the tkg ISO request and Bible translation).

sources.citation: ISO 639-3 Registration Authority. 2010. Change Request 2010-035 (create [tkg] Tesaka Malagasy). SIL International.
sources.note: No linguistic description; lexical-similarity figures only; cites Deschamps 1934, 1936 (ethnography), Deschamps & Vianès 1959, Bouwer 2010.

sources.citation: Rambelo, Michel. 1985. Analyse macro-sociolinguistique d'une situation de diglossie: le cas de Madagascar. Québec: CIRB (Publication H-6), 44 p. ERIC ED266656.
sources.note: Silent. Only dialectological remark (sec. 2.2.1): Dez 1963 and Rajaonarimanana 1977 classify dialects by phonetic criteria; 'certains dialectes du groupe oriental (betsileo, tankarana, tanosy, taisaka) possèdent des traits phonétiques du groupe occidental'.

sources.citation: Elle, Bjørn. 1905. Remarques sur le dialecte Tesaka (ou Taisaka). Bulletin de l'Académie Malgache 4: 124-126.
sources.note: Silent on stress/accent. Three-page missionary note (Farafangana/Vangaindrano): alphabet (no j, s hushing, no tr/dr), final -a/-o > -y, passive imperative -y, lexicon, pronouns, -ka/-tra stems, numerals, conjunction ka, syntax.
No stress or phonology content beyond a note on the absence of Spanish-type 'j' in some words; only bibliographic item is Deschamps 1936.

sources.citation: Deschamps, Hubert. 1936. Le dialecte antaisaka (langue malgache). Thèse complémentaire pour le doctorat ès lettres, Faculté des lettres de Paris. Tananarive: Pitot de la Beaujardière. 126 p.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.access_detail: a digital copy exists, not open: the recorded link leads to a login, a search-only view or a restricted repository; the linked copy is not accessible
sources.note: The only dedicated description of Tesaka (dialect study + Antaisaka-French lexicon + texts); a 1930s French dialect thesis almost certainly has an 'accent' paragraph in its phonetics section. Named by the earlier scan; digitised on Gallica but could not be reached by automated download.
